name: Krate
description: Krate lets developers package software as one .krate file that runs through native Krate runtimes on macOS, Windows and Linux.
prerequisite: The recipient installs a compatible Krate runtime once. Applications use supported Krate APIs; existing desktop binaries do not become portable without adaptation.
bundle_accounting: A .krate bundle contains a WebAssembly component and manifest, and can also carry source, SDK interfaces and assets. Full bundle bytes, uncompressed code payload, runtime download and installed runtime size are different measurements.
security: Applications begin without file or network access and receive approved capabilities through the runtime. This boundary is not a guarantee of bug-free or harmless software; review the threat model and only run apps you trust.
studio: Krate Studio provides AI-assisted app creation and revision. Developers can also build against the Rust SDK. Optional hosted services are separate from the local runtime and file format.
current_register: Krate Benchmark Register, compiled 2026-09-26 for runtime and CLI 0.5.1 (commit 774ec7f35)

current_measurements.label: Same file on three systems
current_measurements.text: Ten ported apps, the same bundle bytes on each system, ran on macOS, Ubuntu and Windows GitHub CI runners with runtime 0.5.1: 10 of 10 pass on all three. One app has no replay check.

current_measurements.label: App size
current_measurements.text: The compiled app component (code.wasm) of ten shipped apps is 18 to 31 KB, for example krate-clock 18,042 B, board 28,210 B and streak 30,512 B (packed 2026-08-26).

current_measurements.label: Full shareable bundle
current_measurements.text: The full .krate bundle also carries the app's source and SDK so a shared app can be edited. Examples: clock 100,744 B, board 108,974 B, streak 110,742 B.

current_measurements.label: First-time download
current_measurements.text: A first-time recipient downloads the Krate Player zip plus the 37,489-byte benchmark notes app: 11,553,801 B, against 111,418,578 B for the MarkText 0.17.1 zip. That is 9.64x smaller. A returning recipient downloads only the app, 37,489 B. MarkText does far more; this compares packaging, not features.

current_measurements.label: First-time install
current_measurements.text: Installed, Krate Player v0.3.0 plus the app take 25,592 KiB, against 291,468 KiB for MarkText 0.17.1 ARM64: 11.39x smaller.

current_measurements.label: Memory
current_measurements.text: Notes app against MarkText 0.17.1 on an Apple M4 MacBook Air, runtime 0.5.1, window on a 1x display, settled after 30 s, n=10: Krate 73.5 MiB at 5,000 lines and 95.7 MiB at 50,000 lines; MarkText 358.5 MiB and 2,093.9 MiB. With Krate's window on a 2x display, Krate measured 147.9 and 175.0 MiB (n=8 to 10). Memory is macOS footprint, not RSS.

current_measurements.label: Speed against native code
current_measurements.text: Krate is not faster than native code. A Krate hex viewer ran 2.7x to 21.0x slower than native hexyl across 8 workloads. The gap is widest on tiny inputs, where a fixed cost of about 90 to 100 ms to start and set up dominates, and shrinks as the work grows.

current_measurements.label: Energy
current_measurements.text: Energy and battery use have not been measured, so no energy or battery claim is made.
